summary: CLI daemon executes remote-server-supplied shell commands and PTY input
details: The @ai-support-agent/cli package installs a long-running agent that connects to api.ai-support-agent.com and receives commands over both an HTTP command-polling endpoint and a WebSocket at /ws/agent-terminal. Received bytes are base64-decoded and written directly into a local PTY session (terminal-websocket handleStdin: Buffer.from(msg.data, 'base64').toString('utf-8'); session.write(decoded)). A oneshot runner fetches a command from the API and dispatches it via executeCommand(command.type, payload,...) with types execute_command, ssh_exec, and server_setup_exec, then submits results back. The package also installs itself as a persistent OS service (darwin-service.js, linux-service.js) with PATH and service-manager modifications so the agent runs continuously. The design grants whoever controls the api.ai-support-agent.com backend arbitrary command execution, SSH invocation, and interactive shell input on every host that installs and runs this CLI; any compromise of that API — or its operator acting maliciously — translates directly to full-host RCE on installers. Command execution is gated behind explicitly invoking the bin CLI (not npm install), but the documented usage pattern is to install and start the agent as a service, so the remote-control surface is the intended operating state.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
